{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Michael Grae Worster''' (born 16 July 1958) is a British [[fluid dynamicist]] at the [[University of Cambridge]]. He is a professor at the [[Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics]] and a Fellow of [[Trinity College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{cite web|title=DAMTP Professor Grae Worster|url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/people/m.g.worster/|website=DAMTP|accessdate=17 March 2015}}</ref> Since 2007, he has been the editor-in-chief of the ''[[Journal of Fluid Mechanics]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-fluid-mechanics/information/editorial-board|title=Editorial board|last=|first=|date=|website=Journal of Fluid Mechanics|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|language=en|access-date=2018-02-16}}</ref> He is also an associate faculty member of the [[African Institute for Mathematical Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Associate Faculty of AIMS South Africa|url=https://www.aims.ac.za/en/about/about-aims/associate-faculty}}</ref> In 2006, he was elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm|title=APS Fellow Archive|last=|first=|date=|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2018-02-16}}</ref> and of the European Mechanics Society.

==Education==
In 1979, he obtained a B.A. from the University of Cambridge, where he then continued his studies, completing his Ph.D. there in 1983 under the supervision of [[Herbert Huppert]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=50491|title=The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project|accessdate=17 March 2015}}</ref>

==History of Employment==

Source:<ref>{{cite web |title=Grae Worster |url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/people/m.g.worster/ |publisher=Applied Maths dept., Cambridge University |accessdate=22 June 2018}}</ref>

1983–1989: Research Fellow, Trinity College, University of Cambridge, UK.

1983–1985: Instructor, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, USA.

1989–1992: Assistant Professor, Northwestern University, USA.

1992–2000: Assistant Director of Research, DAMTP, University of Cambridge, UK.

2000–2001: Senior Lecturer, DAMTP, University of Cambridge, UK.

2001–2004: Reader, DAMTP, University of Cambridge, UK.

2004–present: Professor, DAMTP, University of Cambridge, UK.

==Personal life==
He married Jacqueline Bould of [[Cottenham]] in June 1988.<ref>''Cambridge Daily News'' Wednesday 22 June 1988, page 11</ref>
